title: Adjoint mates on cartesian derived sections
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with a fixed compactification $f=pj$. For $W=X,Y$ let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves on the small pro-etale site: an object has maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$, and morphisms commute with these maps. Use its ordinary unbounded derived category and its exact evaluations $e_n$. Let $\mathscr N_W$ be the full subcategory of normalized systems, meaning that every transition-adjoint $t^M_{m,n}:M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ is invertible, whose individual levels lie in $D^b_{ctf}(W,A_n)$. No uniform cohomological or Tor interval is imposed in this notation.

The ordinary system compact-support functor $\mathcal F_f=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ restricts to $\mathscr N_X\to\mathscr N_Y$. It has a right adjoint $\mathcal E_f:\mathscr N_Y\to\mathscr N_X$, constructed from a right adjoint on the ambient derived category of strict etale systems and etale/pro-etale comparison; existence of $\mathcal E_f$ is a conclusion. There are specified natural identifications
$$e_n\mathcal F_f\cong F_n e_n,\qquad e_n\mathcal E_f\cong G_n e_n,$$
where $F_n=Rf_{!,A_n}$ and $G_n=Rf^!_{A_n}$ are the finite constructible adjoints, with their specified units $\eta_n$ and counits $\epsilon_n$. These identifications preserve the counits, hence the units. If $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ and $q_{m,n}:T^Y_{m,n}F_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nT^X_{m,n}$ is the canonical compact-support comparison, the reduction transitions are
$$t^{\mathcal F_fM}_{m,n}=F_n(t^M_{m,n})q_{m,n,M_m},\qquad t^{\mathcal E_fN}_{m,n}=G_n(t^N_{m,n})b_{m,n,N_m},$$
where $b_{m,n}$ is the $F_n\dashv G_n$ transpose of $T^Y_{m,n}(\epsilon_m)q_{m,n,G_m}^{-1}$. It is the canonical invertible finite comparison of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. The unit and counit are actual morphisms of ordinary derived systems and satisfy the triangle identities there.

For $M\in\mathscr N_X$, $N\in\mathscr N_Y$, use the fiberwise mapping systems $\mathcal H_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. There is a specified natural isomorphism
$$\Phi_{M,N}:\mathcal H_Y(\mathcal F_fM,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_X(M,\mathcal E_fN)\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab})).$$
It is constructed by the ordinary system tensor-Hom adjunction, the compact-support projection formula and the actual system counit. Its evaluation is the finite derived mapping-complex adjunction; on degree-zero Hom its maps are $h\mapsto\mathcal E_f(h)\eta_M$ and $g\mapsto\epsilon_N\mathcal F_f(g)$. Applying $R\lim$ gives an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. Units, counits, evaluation transposes and inverse identities are specified before taking $R\lim$. The construction respects ordinary mates of specified transformations of the actual system compact-support functors, in particular geometric composition comparisons. Tensor-evaluation and tensor-Hom transposes built from these actual maps and derived system tensors are system maps with the corresponding finite evaluations.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1-3: uniqueness of the right adjoint, enriched mapping adjunction, and counit transposes. The enhanced adjoint recognition and descent assertion is an additional agent-formulated categorical lemma. Ordinary mate prototype: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change); that tag does not assert enhanced descent.

proof.text: First work on the small etale sites. Denote their strict $A_\bullet$-module system categories by $\mathscr S_W^{\mathrm{et}}$. They are module categories on the ringed topos of inverse sequences, hence Grothendieck abelian by the ringed-site theorem. The ordinary system inverse/direct-image theorem constructs $P_u\dashv S_u=Ru_{*,\bullet}$ on unbounded derived categories, with $e_nS_u\cong Ru_{*,n}e_n$ including the evaluated units and counits. Exact open extension $J_j\dashv P_j$ applies termwise. Thus $F=S_pJ_j$ is an actual exact functor on $D(\mathscr S_X^{\mathrm{et}})$ and $e_nF=F_n^{\mathrm{et}}e_n$ on this entire unbounded category. No assertion on unrestricted pro-etale compact supports is needed.

source.place: Ordinary ringed system operations; preparation for the middle RHom calculation

proof.text: For a family $(K_i)$ the canonical sum map $\bigoplus_i FK_i\to F(\bigoplus_i K_i)$ evaluates to the corresponding finite compact-support sum map: $J_j$ preserves sums because it is a left adjoint, and proper etale derived direct image preserves sums for module coefficients. Evaluations are exact and coproducts of systems are levelwise, so this map is an isomorphism. Brown representability for the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category now gives $F\dashv G$ on the ambient etale system categories. Its unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$ already are natural derived system maps with triangle identities.

source.place: Brown construction of the system adjunction; Stacks 0F5Y and etale-cohomology Tag 0F0D

proof.text: Put $L_n=LE_n\dashv e_n$ as in the coefficient-evaluation theorem. Thus $(L_nK)_r=K\otimes^L_{A_n}A_r$ for $r\le n$, zero otherwise; in particular $e_nL_n=1$. Use its actual maps $\sigma_{m,n}:L_nT_{m,n}\to L_m$. The system tensor operations, including their projection maps, are formed on the ringed sequence site by K-flat resolutions and the inverse-image/direct-image counits. The proper projection map for $S_p$ evaluates to the finite etale projection map, which is invertible on all unbounded finite-coefficient inputs. Exact open extension has its tensor comparison. Consequently the actual compact-support projection map is invertible on the etale system category, by conservative evaluation. Applying it to a constant coefficient module $A_r$ also gives the unbounded finite coefficient-change maps $q_{n,r}$. The coefficient-change target is the ordinary etale one: derived extension and exact restriction are adjoint, and their commutation with geometric pullback identifies the two composites of right adjoints by counit-compatible uniqueness. Open extension commutes with restriction termwise. Thus the projection with $A_r$ gives the changed-coefficient compact support, not merely its underlying $A_n$-complex.

Define $a_n:L_n^YF_n^{\mathrm{et}}\to FL_n^X$ as the $L_n^Y\dashv e_n^Y$ transpose of the identity $F_n^{\mathrm{et}}=e_n^YFL_n^X$. This is an actual system transformation. At $r\le n$ its component is the coefficient-change projection $q_{n,r}$, by the counit definition of that projection; above $n$ both sides vanish. Thus $a_n$ is invertible. The maps $a_n$ also respect the $\sigma_{m,n}$: explicitly the two maps from $L_nF_nT^X_{m,n}$ to $FL_m$ are $F(\sigma^X_{m,n})a_n$ and $a_m\sigma^Y_{m,n}L_n(q_{m,n}^{-1})$. Under $L_n^Y\dashv e_n^Y$ both transpose to $q_{m,n}^{-1}$, using the displayed formula for precomposition with $\sigma$ in the evaluation theorem. Equality follows from this adjunction bijection, without faithfulness of evaluation on arbitrary maps.

source.place: Derived free insertion comparisons and their truncation compatibility

proof.text:
For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$ and $N\in D(\mathscr S_Y^{\mathrm{et}})$ compute naturally
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K,e_nGN)=\operatorname{Hom}(L_nK,GN)=\operatorname{Hom}(FL_nK,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_nF_nK,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_nK,N_n).$$
The final functor is represented by the finite etale right adjoint $G_n^{\mathrm{et}}N_n$ (the same Brown argument at one level). Yoneda gives a natural isomorphism $\theta_n:e_nG\cong G_n^{\mathrm{et}}e_n$. Fix precisely this isomorphism. The defining equality identifies the evaluated counit with $\epsilon_n$; uniqueness of the counit-compatible identification of right adjoints leaves no choice of signs or automorphisms. The existing etale coefficient-system adjoint theorem supplies these same ambient finite adjoints and counit-compatible evaluations. On finite constructible inputs their pro-etale transports are exactly the definition of $Rf_n^!$; finite-Tor preservation is a separate theorem, used next.

source.place: Identification of the levels by representability, not a lift of finite functors

proof.text:
Precompose the Hom calculation of the preceding step with $\sigma_{m,n}$. The evaluation theorem says that on its left this is $h\mapsto t^{GN}_{m,n}T^X_{m,n}(h)$. On its right the compatibility of $a$ with $\sigma$ says that it is $h\mapsto t^N_{m,n}T^Y_{m,n}(h)q_{m,n}^{-1}$. Transposing by $F_n\dashv G_n$ therefore identifies the actual reduction map of $GN$ with
$$G_n(t^N_{m,n})b_{m,n,N_m},\qquad b_{m,n}=G_n(T^Y_{m,n}\epsilon_m)G_n(q_{m,n,G_m}^{-1})\eta_{n,T^X_{m,n}G_m}.$$
This identity is determined on every test $K$ in the Hom calculation, hence by Yoneda. Changing from the Brown finite adjoints to the specified constructible ones conjugates this formula by their counit-compatible isomorphisms, exactly as in the unique-adjoint coefficient theorem. Evaluating the actual unit gives $\eta_n$ too: under the same Hom calculation it is the transpose of $1_{F_nM_n}$.

source.place: Transitions and unit from the derived evaluation adjunctions

proof.text: On bounded constructible finite-Tor levels, the finite exceptional theorem identifies this $b$ with its canonical invertible coefficient comparison and supplies the two unit/counit mate identities. The compact-support comparisons $q$ and the formula for the reduction maps of $F$ are the projection comparisons of the system operations. Consequently normalized inputs are sent to normalized outputs by both $F$ and $G$: their reduction maps are composites of the displayed invertible maps. Finite constructibility and finite Tor amplitude are preserved separately at each $n$ by exact open extension followed by proper finite direct image, and by the finite exceptional preservation theorem. For the former use lem-trf-open-ctf and cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale on the finite-dimensional compactification; for the latter use thm-sf-preservation-class. No uniform bound is used. This restricts the actual ambient adjunction to the stated full subcategories. These are the levelwise-finite subcategories in the statement, not the uniformly bounded subcategories of sk-def-sp-normalized-towers.

source.place: Restriction to normalized finite-Tor constructible systems

proof.text: The mate cocycle can also be checked independently. For $k\ge m\ge n$, transpose $b_{m,n,T_{k,m}N}T_{m,n}(b_{k,m,N})$ under $F_n\dashv G_n$. Ordinary mate pasting gives the composite $T_{m,n}T_{k,m}\epsilon_k$ after $q_{k,m}^{-1}$ and $q_{m,n}^{-1}$. Coefficient associativity and the cocycle of $q$ identify it with the transpose of $b_{k,n,N}$. For $m=n$ the mate word is $G_n\epsilon_n\,\eta_nG_n=1$. This proves the cocycle and identity indices using finite adjunctions. The finite exceptional theorem gives the same canonical cocycle.

The system triangle identities hold because $\eta,\epsilon$ were obtained with the Brown adjunction, before restricting objects or evaluating. Explicitly the Hom transposes are $h\mapsto G(h)\eta_M$ and $g\mapsto\epsilon_NF(g)$; their composites reduce by naturality to $h\epsilon_{FM}F\eta_M=h$ and $G\epsilon_N\eta_{GN}g=g$. These are equations in the ambient ordinary derived category of systems. They remain equations on the full normalized subcategories.

source.place: Actual unit/counit and triangle identities before total limit

proof.text:
Apply the unbounded system inverse/direct-image construction to $
u_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}	o W_{\mathrm{et}}$. The unit and counit are actual system maps; their evaluations are the finite site-comparison maps. Unbounded finite-coefficient full faithfulness implies that the system unit is invertible. For any system whose every level has etale origin, the counit is likewise invertible, by conservative evaluation. Thus $
u_W^*$ identifies $D(\mathscr S_W^{\mathrm{et}})$ with the full subcategory of pro-etale derived systems with etale-origin levels. Finite constructible levels have this origin. The actual compact-support comparison $
u_Y^*F	o Rp_{*, ullet}J_j
u_X^*$ is the proper direct-image mate after exact open extension. Its evaluations are invertible by unbounded etale/pro-etale direct-image comparison. Transfer the adjunction and its specified maps along these equivalences. This constructs $\mathcal F_f,\mathcal E_f$ on every system in $\mathscr N$, without a common bound and without postulating a pro-etale ambient exceptional adjoint.

source.place: Etale-origin realization of the normalized pro-etale system adjunction

proof.text:
We next identify the mapping systems using closed adjunctions on the ordinary ringed sequence sites. For normalized $M$ and arbitrary $N$, let $H^{\mathrm{sys}}_W(M,N)$ be their ringed-site derived internal Hom. Its $n$th evaluation is the finite derived internal Hom. Indeed for a test $K$ on the level-$n$ site the canonical tensor map $L_n(K\otimes^LM_n)\to L_nK\otimes^LM$ is invertible: at $r\le n$ this is normalization of $M$ and tensor associativity, and above $n$ both are zero. The map is the $L_n\dashv e_n$ transpose of the level-$n$ identity, so exists before evaluation. The closed and evaluation adjunctions give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K,e_nH^{\mathrm{sys}}(M,N))=\operatorname{Hom}(L_nK\otimes^LM,N)=\operatorname{Hom}(K\otimes^LM_n,N_n).$$
For internal sheaf Hom apply this calculation also on each localized site; the same ringed-site statements apply there. Yoneda gives the asserted finite internal-Hom identification, preserving evaluation.

The evaluation calculus supplies an actual system map $\mathcal I_W(M,N)\otimes^LM\to N$. Its closed transpose gives $\mathcal I_W(M,N)\to H^{\mathrm{sys}}_W(M,N)$; the preceding finite-Hom identification shows every evaluation is the identity, so this map is invertible. For normalized etale inputs, the pullback tensor map and evaluation similarly transpose to an actual comparison $\nu_W^*H^{\mathrm{sys}}_{W,\mathrm{et}}\to H^{\mathrm{sys}}_{W,\mathrm{proet}}$. Its evaluations are invertible by thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible: the first input is finite-Tor and both inputs are bounded constructible at each level. Thus the pro-etale Hom system has etale origin.
Carry out the representing calculation on etale systems. Since $s_{\mathrm{et}}$ is punctual, $\widehat{\mathcal H}_W=Ra_{W,*,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}H^{\mathrm{sys}}_{W,\mathrm{et}}(M,N)$ is an ordinary derived $A_\bullet$-module system, representing
$$P\longmapsto\operatorname{Hom}(a_W^*P\otimes^LM,N).$$
This uses the closed and inverse/direct-image adjunctions. The site-comparison unit and derived pushforward composition identify its image in abelian-group towers with the pro-etale mapping system $\mathcal H_W$. Global sections on the pro-etale coefficient point are taken here, not silently identified with forgetting coefficients.

source.place: Identify the specified fiberwise mapping systems by their actual evaluation maps

proof.text:
For an arbitrary test coefficient system $P$ on $s$, the system projection isomorphism constructed above gives $a_Y^*P\otimes^LFM\cong F(a_X^*P\otimes^LM)$. Hence
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,\widehat{\mathcal H}_Y(FM,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(a_Y^*P\otimes^LFM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F(a_X^*P\otimes^LM),N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(a_X^*P\otimes^LM,GN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,\widehat{\mathcal H}_X(M,GN)).$$
Every bijection is an actual system adjunction or the system projection isomorphism. It is natural for all $P$, so Yoneda gives a specified mapping-system isomorphism with inverse. Restriction to abelian-group towers gives $\Phi$. The inverse equations follow from the inverse representing bijections, in the ordinary derived category of coefficient systems; no equality is inferred from finite evaluations.

source.place: Middle RHom adjunction as an isomorphism of ordinary derived systems

proof.text: The representing bijections use the actual counit $FGN\to N$ and projection map, so their finite evaluations are the ordinary finite tensor-Hom/counit transposes. This can be read by testing on $L_nP_n$ in the same calculation, rather than lifting a finite transpose. The counit-compatible identifications already fix the finite adjunctions; the standard finite internal adjunction and site comparison identify their derived mapping-complex maps with those in the statement. At degree-zero Hom the forward and inverse maps are $h\mapsto G(h)\eta_M$ and $g\mapsto\epsilon_NF(g)$ by the actual adjunction. Their inverse identities were proved as system identities in the representing calculation.

source.place: Specified finite evaluations of the system mapping adjunction

proof.text: Apply the total derived inverse-limit functor to $\Phi$ and its already specified inverse. A functor preserves compositions and identities, so their images are inverse isomorphisms in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. Naturality and the evaluation/transpose identities are carried along by the same functor.

source.place: Pass to total derived inverse limit only after constructing the system isomorphism

proof.text: For a specified ordinary transformation between system compact-support functors, take its ordinary adjunction mate using the actual units and counits above. Its evaluation is the finite mate because the identifications preserve those units and counits. For composition comparisons use the composite adjunction; ordinary mate pasting gives the horizontal and vertical composition laws as equalities of derived system transformations. Counit-compatible uniqueness identifies different choices of ambient right adjoints. Thus this applies to the geometric composition maps used by the citers. It makes no claim of lifting transformations specified only at the finite levels.

source.place: Naturality and composition by ordinary system mates

proof.text: Finally form tensors on flat-term K-flat system resolutions. K-flat existence, the flat-term K-flat total-tensor model and the ringed-site closed structure make these operations and their evaluation transposes independent of representatives. Composing their actual system maps with $\eta,\epsilon$ and using the system closed-adjunction bijection produces actual tensor-Hom transposes. Evaluation of those composites and bijections is the finite construction by the preceding internal-Hom identification. Their compatibility with transitions is therefore a property of these constructed system maps, rather than a criterion for lifting unrelated finite maps.

source.place: Tensor-evaluation transposes on ordinary system resolutions; Stacks 06YS, 08J9, 0A95
